transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. It may be damaged, yes. Do not use it again until a qualified microwave engineer has checked it. With it unplugged, you can safely inspect the cavity only: look for scorch marks, melted plastic, burnt residue, or a browned/burnt small flat cover panel on an inside wall or roof. Do not remove the casing or any internal cover.

There was some smoke coming out of the vents at the side when we stopped it, and a hot electrical burnt smell. I've turned it off at the switch but it's still plugged in - should I unplug it now? Is it safe to keep or should I bin it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If there are flames or smoke is still coming from it, keep away, don't open the door of an oven, microwave or dryer that is on fire, switch it off at the wall or the fuse box only if you can do that safely, get everyone out and call 999.
There's no flames and the smoke has stopped, it's just the smell now. So should I unplug it at the wall? And is it worth getting it repaired or should I just bin it? It's only a £60 Bush from Argos.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes — unplug it at the wall now, provided the plug and socket area are cool and there is no remaining smoke. Leave it unplugged and do not run it again, even with water in it, as smoke and an electrical burning smell after being run empty can mean damage to the microwave’s internal high-voltage parts or a burnt internal cover panel. For a £60 microwave, a professional microwave repair is usually unlikely to be economical, and it must not go in normal household rubbish: take it to a local electrical/WEEE recycling point or retailer recycling scheme. If you prefer to keep it, it needs assessment by a qualified microwave repair engineer first; do not remove the casing yourself.

plan: They asked: "Is it broken?" - answer that first.

Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "horrible smell after running empty". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
